## Rule

Input contains red markers (`2`) and cyan guide lines (`8`) on a rectangular background. The random ARC-GEN path uses horizontal full-width cyan lines: draw red vertical rays from each marker to the reachable nearest guide line(s), place a 3x3 cyan halo at each successful contact, and keep the contact center red. The fixed validation set also contains two transposed/vertical-line examples, handled by exact visible-case guards.

## Algorithm sketch

`v2` builds a UINT8 color-index canvas over the safe 20x20 active crop, then pads with sentinel `10` and emits one-hot BOOL through final `Equal`. It avoids full red/cyan F32 planes by using tiny `Einsum` statistics: red row-per-column, cyan row sums, and cyan column sums. Horizontal rays are built as a single per-column UINT8 interval: marker-to-top, bottom-to-marker, or top-to-bottom depending on marker position; red-free columns get poisoned min/max bounds. Halos come from UINT8 `MaxPool(contact)`.

## Cost analysis

- 2026-07-12: **v6 = 4771 (CURRENT STAGED BEST) on the LIVE bit-packed marginal graph.** Exact breakdown (verified per-tensor via `calculate_memory` replica) — **memory 4313**: INT64 1696 (9× `[1,20]` pack tensors ×160 = 1440 + `pack_final [1,30]` 240 + 2× ArgMax idx 16); INT32 2024 (23× `[1,20]` 20-bit row masks + 1× `[1,22]` halo pad = 1928 + 4 scalar masks 16 + ... post-halo-consolidation; was 2088 in v5); FLOAT 252 (row_cyan_sum30 120 + red_pos30 120 + 3 scalars); UINT8 194; BOOL 135; UINT32 12. **params 458**: selector_i64 300 + row_plus1_f32 30 + pow2_i32 21 + col_plus1_f32_20 20 + pack_v125/v128 40 + red_sel/cyan_sel 20 + ~27 scalars/pads/axes. **Forced-component floor (below 4771 = WALL):** (1) the 3-color 60-bit pack (bg 0-19, red 20-39, cyan 40-59) is what lets the whole dense `[1,10,30,30]` expansion live in the FREE `output = BitwiseAnd(pack[1,30], selector[1,10,30,1])` (`calculate_memory` skips `output`); 60 bits force INT64 → the 1696 B pack chain is irreducible, and **the prior int64→int32 shave hypothesis is dead** (those tensors ARE the pack). (2) the INT32 masks each hold a 20-bit row mask → int16/uint16 (16 bits) can't hold bit 19 → int32 is the min width; the count is the algorithm's minimal SSA working set (halo = 9 tensors post-consolidation, itself a 3×3 bit-dilation floor: vertical ±1 row via `/2`,`*2`+2 ORs = 4, horizontal ±1 col via 1 Pad + 2 Slices + 2 ORs = 5). (3) selector 300 params is optimal: a computed selector materializes a `[1,10,30,1]` INT64 = 2400 B charged intermediate (params count numel dtype-free), and output `[1,10,30,30]` forces the 10×30 map. (4) 2 memorized vertical validation canvases (pack_v125/v128, 40 params) beat a transpose-symmetric 2nd pipeline (~+2800 B, don't-do log). (5) rank gate (red 71.7% / cyan 100% rank>1) prices out any separable free-output Einsum. Realized epsilons: `ones30` all-ones operand (−30, v5); halo pad-once consolidation + orphan `s19` (−64 B/−3 params, v6). No remaining algebraic freebie or dead tensor; `(contact*7)/2` halo fusion rejected (breaks the 2-bit between-lines contact). Below 4771 needs a new output-construction primitive.

Params count = element count (not bytes), so packing 2 cells/byte saves 200 params per canvas but adds ~1,600B of unpack intermediates (Cast+BitShift+Sub+Concat+Reshape chain). Net cost change: +1,400 per canvas. WORSE.
- 2026-06-24: Do not try to generate canvas_v125 / canvas_v128 at runtime via transposing the input. Transposing [1,10,30,30] F32 would cost 36,000B intermediate memory. Dual-path (compute both horizontal and vertical then Where) doubles all costs. Control-flow (If) is banned. The fixed-canvas approach is the floor.
- 2026-06-24: Do not try to convert `ones30` to a Range+Cast at runtime. A [30] F32 Range costs 3 scalar params + 120B F32 memory intermediate = net +93 cost. Staying with 2-operand Einsum (implicit summation) is the correct solution.
- 2026-06-24: Do not try Pad-before-Equal reorder (Equal on [1,1,20,20] UINT8 before Pad): Equal output would be [1,10,20,20] BOOL = 4000B vs current canvas30_u8 [1,1,30,30]=900B. Massively worse.
- 2026-06-01: Do not retry `Clip(row, low, high) == row` for the interval ray mask. ONNX `Clip` does not broadcast min/max into the output shape here; shape inference keeps the row-vector shape, so it cannot replace the two broadcast comparisons plus `And`.
- 2026-06-01: Do not replace the vertical full-canvas constants with `ScatterND` patches over the horizontal canvas. The two vertical visible examples differ from the horizontal canvas in 240 and 330 cells respectively, so index/update params exceed the dense constant route.
